title: Netanyahu orders military to plan evacuation of Rafah
body:
On 9 February 2024, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said he had ordered the military to prepare a plan to evacuate hundreds of thousands of displaced Palestinians from Rafah ahead of a ground invasion. He gave no details or timeline. His office said it was impossible to achieve the goal of eliminating Hamas while leaving four Hamas battalions in Rafah, and Netanyahu framed clearing the city as necessary for total victory over the group.

More than half of Gaza's 2.3 million people were packed into Rafah, on the border with Egypt, many displaced several times. The UN put the number of people there at 1.4 million and said forced displacement would be out of line. UN humanitarian chief Martin Griffiths asked where people were supposed to go. The United States said it could not support an operation there without a proper humanitarian plan, and Washington, other allies and rights groups warned an invasion would be a disaster.

Overnight into Saturday 10 February, three Israeli air raids on Rafah killed at least 28 people, according to Al Jazeera, with each raid reportedly killing multiple members of three families, including 10 children. Al Jazeera cited a toll of about 28,000 Palestinians killed in the war. Detailed plans were presented to Israel's war cabinet later in February, and Israel's offensive on Rafah began in May 2024.
